text: Have you ever thought about dating a vampire?
Hollywood says cheekbones and a velvet coat.
Folklore says a swollen corpse, red in the face, who died last Tuesday.
Let's say you date one anyway.
Day one. He won't come in until you invite him. So old-fashioned.
The invitation doesn't expire. He's in your kitchen at four a.m.
Day two. Every couple photo is just you, and a floating rose.
Day three. He doesn't eat. He watches you eat. Mostly your neck.
Day four. You drop a bag of rice.
He has to count every grain. At nine thousand, he lost his place.
Day five. He stays over. He's brought a crate of his own soil.
Day six. No picnics. In the book, Dracula went out at noon.
A film in nineteen twenty-two changed the rules. Now the curtains are taped shut.
Day seven. Your anniversary. He says you look pale.
You do. And there are two small marks on your neck.
It shows the bathroom. And a rose, floating where your hand should be.
